Lesson 12.4 · 49 of 78 · 25 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Portfolio measures, regulatory returns and lineage

After this lesson you can:
  • Define portfolio measures without denominator ambiguity
  • Trace report fields to source events
  • Specify filing, rejection and amendment workflows

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Metric contracts
  2. Reporting is a controlled lifecycle
  3. Lineage to the borrower
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Metric contracts

Disbursement, outstanding, overdue, collection efficiency, PAR, GNPA, yield, vintage loss and roll rate need population, as-of time, numerator, denominator, exclusions and currency.

A dashboard label is not a definition.

Segment dimensions and late-arriving corrections must be consistent across risk, finance and operations.

2. Reporting is a controlled lifecycle

CIC, CIMS/DLA, CKYCRR, FIU, CERSAI, CRILC, PSL and statutory returns differ in scope and format but share prepare, validate, maker-checker, submit, acknowledge, reject/repair, amend and archive states. A generated file without acknowledgement is not a completed filing.

3. Lineage to the borrower

Each submitted field should trace to a source fact or event, transformation version and submission batch.

Corrections propagate to source, affected reports and borrower communication.

Evidence includes approvals, hash, transport response and reconciled totals.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-CIR-2025 — CIC reporting has schedules, reject repair and correction clocks.
  • RBI-DLA-CIMS — DLA reporting requires certification and current public inventory.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. When is a regulatory submission complete?

  1. When the file is generated
  2. After authorised submission, acknowledgement and reconciliation under the return's rules
  3. When a dashboard turns green
  4. At period end
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Generation is only one state in a controlled filing lifecycle.
